hits.full_text:
A Monday morning question for you: 

Life is always progressing to the next stage. As you enter a new season, habits that previously served you well may need to be refreshed or adjusted. Which one of your current habits have you outgrown and is in need of a change?
hits.hook: JamesClear: Monday question, which habit have you outgrown as you enter a new season (replies locked; post or quote angle)
hits.draft_en:
Some habits don't fail. They just finish their job.

What carried me through a hard stretch isn't always what I need now. I don't have to be mad at it. I can thank it, set it down, and try something smaller.

Which one are you ready to set down?
hits.video_tip: 15 seconds, overhead on textured cream paper, window light, room sound only. A hand uncaps a fountain pen, crosses out one line on a short habit list, writes a smaller one underneath, caps the pen. No face. Last frame text: 'Thank it. Set it down.'

hits.full_text: Life advice I learned from sports: Entitlement erodes respect faster than failure. Nobody owes you anything. Special treatment. Softer rules. Automatic recognition. Whatever. You have to win your spot. Be grateful for every opportunity to do so. Respect is earned, not given.

hits.draft_en:
Nobody owes me an audience for building something. That's fine.

I'd rather earn it the slow way. Show the work. Keep the promises small. Then actually keep them.

reply_ideas.reply_text: The quiet version of this is just showing up when nobody's handing out credit yet. The spot gets earned in the boring reps, long before anyone notices.
Failing in front of people stings for a week. Acting like you're owed the room costs you for years. I'll take the first one every time.
"Deal with the two feet right in front of you" is the part I needed. The big plan gets loud fast. Two feet, I can manage.
Six months sounds short until week three, when nothing looks different yet. That's the week I try to plan for. Small enough to keep doing when it's boring.

x_posts.title: Quiet reps: the two-hundredth page
x_posts.text:
Nobody claps for the two-hundredth page.

The first entry in a new notebook feels like an event. By month four it's a pen, a few lines, and nobody asking how it's going.

That quiet stretch is where anything actually changes.
x_posts.why: Outsider pattern: the first rep gets a post, the 200th gets silence (maxroeck) + journaling comebacks; pairs with Bloom's earn-your-spot STAR

x_posts.title: Missed days are information
x_posts.text:
A rule I'm keeping for the notebook: missed days are information, not a bill.

No fake catch-up entry. No starting over next Monday. The next honest line counts, even if it's just "haven't written in a while."

That's enough to pick it back up.
